pr_title: [ML] remove thread sleep from results persister
pr_body:
Having a thread sleep in a recurring action may cause issues on node shutdown.
What if the thread is sleeping while a nice shutdown is occurring? Since these retry timeouts
can extend to a larger period of time, we should instead use scheduled tasks + the threadpool.
This allows the retries to be effectively canceled instead of waiting for a thread to wake back up.

closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/65890
pr_comments: I had a quick look and I really like this change! As other reviewers have jumped in, I'm happy when you all are happy :-)

issue_context.title: [ML] ResultsPersisterService may delay the node to close
issue_context.body:
Our `ResultsPersisterService` achieves scheduling the next retry by calling `Thread.sleep`. This is dodgy as it blocks a thread and may cause the node to delay closing down. This has manifested in a CI failure in #65710.

We should refactor it to use the thread pool and schedule the next retry instead of sleeping.
comments: We should also investigate reusing `RetryableAction` if possible.

@benwtrent I hit another failure on this despite the fix that went in. It still looks like the results persister service keeps retrying despite the node closing. The failure is here https://elasticsearch-ci.elastic.co/job/elastic+elasticsearch+pull-request-2/14332/testReport/junit/org.elasticsearch.xpack.ml.integration/MlDistributedFailureIT/testClusterWithTwoMlNodes_RunsDatafeed_GivenOriginalNodeGoesDown/.

Look for `test-node-goes-down-while-running-job` and notice how `node_t3` keeps retrying to persist `data_counts` after we initiated shutdown for the node.

review_comments:
I'm not convinced this class is bringing much to the party. 

`private volatile BulkRequest bulkRequest;` could be a field in `BulkRetryableAction` and `buildNewRequestFromFailures` could be called directly.

>could be a field in BulkRetryableAction and buildNewRequestFromFailures could be called directly.

No, it cannot. Because the action is passed via `super` the `super` is ctor'd before the child class is. So, references DIRECTLY to the child class methods is not possible.

This class guaruntees things are constructed and mutable inside the lambda passed to super.
Good catch, it was sending the wrong `bulkRequest` before
I don't understand why this is now required. Does it have to be part of this change?
I noticed log spam when it wasn't around. This and the other changes (including more plugins) got rid of a bunch of log spam for the single node tests.
